access_method: Direct read-only opens of the exact public primary-source URLs below through the web retrieval tool. No code, local audio, product, account, or live service was run.

sources.title: RFC 8493: The BagIt File Packaging Format (V1.0)
sources.publisher: RFC Editor / IETF Datatracker; Independent Submission
sources.version_or_commit: RFC 8493, BagIt v1.0, October 2018; Informational RFC, not Internet Standards Track
sources.locator: Sections 1.1 and 2.1.2-2.1.3 (arbitrary opaque payload and required payload manifests); sections 2.2.1 and 5.4 (optional tag manifests and active-attack boundary)
sources.observed_operation: Opened the RFC HTML and inspected its purpose, status, payload, manifest and security sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Each bag requires at least one payload manifest, and each such manifest lists every payload file exactly once. Tag-file encoding SHOULD be UTF-8. A tag manifest is optional. Payload checksums provide corruption confidence and are not designed against active attacks.
sources.applicability: Supports a portable opaque-file transfer/fixity package for audio, notes, photos and derivatives. A payload manifest covers payload files, not automatically every BagIt tag file; it does not establish semantic metadata, consent or authority.

sources.title: Guidelines: Embedding Metadata in Broadcast WAVE Files
sources.version_or_commit: Live guide identifies Version 3, approved 2021-04-26; no commit applies
sources.locator: Current-version and scope sections; MetaEdit support and guideline description
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official FADGI guide and inspected its stated BWF scope, current version and linked PDF.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The guidance is for metadata embedded in Broadcast WAVE, not every WAV recorder or application. It describes embedded metadata as potentially synergistic with organizational databases; it does not make embedded metadata the authority.
sources.applicability: Supports keeping an optional embedded subset alongside an organizational record, while leaving the society's field authority as an owner choice.

sources.title: Guidelines for Embedding Metadata in Broadcast WAVE Files
sources.publisher: Federal Agencies Digital Guidelines Initiative Audio-Visual Working Group
sources.locator: PDF pp. 8-12 (BEXT field/version/date conditions), pp. 22-24 (cue/adtl/ltxt, purpose tran, cue-range association, ASCII and RIFF termination/padding)
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official PDF and inspected BEXT field definitions, origination-time guidance, and the ltxt Purpose and text conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guidance is scoped to Broadcast WAVE embedding and distinguishes recommended, optional and required elements. ltxt may use purpose tran for transcription, but the text is ASCII and associated with cue ranges; RIFF null termination and padding conditions apply. FADGI describes origination time as local to the archival entity.
sources.applicability: Supports an optional constrained BWF subset and the draft's caution against placing a complete UTF-8 transcript or rich descriptive prose in such fields. Does not establish compatibility of volunteer files or target applications.

sources.title: EBU Tech 3285 v2: Broadcast Wave Format Specification
sources.locator: PDF pp. 7-8 (BWF version compatibility and additional chunk handling), pp. 8-9 (BEXT structure and ASCII field constraints)
sources.observed_operation: Opened the EBU PDF and inspected version compatibility, section 2.1 chunk handling and BEXT field descriptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Older BWF readers may ignore later-version UMID/loudness values. Unspecified additional chunks need not be interpreted or used and their content integrity is not guaranteed; BWF-compliant applications shall pass those chunks. Optional chunks are not supported by all applications.
sources.applicability: Primary evidence for distinguishing reader support from writer pass-through expectations. It does not guarantee preservation of unknown chunks by arbitrary WAV software or prove the behavior of a selected editor.

sources.title: BWF MetaEdit project page
sources.version_or_commit: Live project page listed Version 26.08.1 at access; page does not pin its help text to a code commit
sources.locator: Lines 38-55 (BWF-only scope and platform binaries), 59-69 (listed version, metadata operations and audio-data MD5)
sources.observed_operation: Opened and searched the official project page for current version, platforms, operations, checksum scope and GUI/CLI wording.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page says the tool edits BWF files, lists binaries for multiple platforms, imports/edits/embeds/exports specified metadata and applies MD5 to the WAVE data chunk only. The opened page does not say GUI or CLI.
sources.applicability: Supports BWF MetaEdit as a candidate for a conditional working-copy workflow and the audio-only digest limit. It does not validate a local file or support the draft's interface-mode wording at this locator.

sources.title: BWF MetaEdit help: CORE Document
sources.version_or_commit: Unversioned rolling help page; documentation commit unavailable
sources.locator: Lines 37-56 (exchange behavior, one record per audio file, filepath association and CSV field parameters)
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official help page and inspected exchange purpose, record/path association and CSV parameters.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CORE exchanges BEXT/LIST-INFO between MetaEdit and other applications as XML or CSV; it lists one record per audio file and associates values with filepaths. Several BEXT columns have ASCII character limits.
sources.applicability: Supports the proposed optional exchange workflow while showing why filepaths alone are not enduring object identifiers. Rolling documentation is not a version-specific round-trip test.

sources.title: BWF MetaEdit help: LIST-INFO Audio Metadata Information
sources.version_or_commit: Unversioned rolling help page; documentation commit unavailable
sources.locator: Lines 70 and 86 (embedded metadata may not be latest/best; follow identifiers for later/better data)
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official help page and inspected its stale-metadata guidance and identifier pointer.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page warns that embedded metadata may not represent the latest and best information and recommends following identifiers for later or better data.
sources.applicability: Supports, but does not mandate, a linked authoritative external descriptive record.

sources.title: BWF MetaEdit help: XML Chunks
sources.version_or_commit: Unversioned rolling help page; documentation commit unavailable
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official help page and inspected its XML validation and undo warning.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The current page says the editor does not verify entered aXML/iXML/XMP data as valid XML or valid instances and has no undo for those edits.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft's specific caution for these editor functions; not a universal statement about every WAV editor or chunk.

sources.title: BWF MetaEdit GUI release history
sources.locator: Lines 6-15 (26.08/25.04), lines 42-46 (23.04 encodings/CSET), lines 72-81 (21.07 UNICODE=1 XML import), lines 268-276 (0.2.2 CR/special-character and complete-file-write issues)
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official raw repository history and inspected the named release entries. No immutable commit was exposed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: These are release-history entries for named tool versions, not current behavior of every application or version. The branch is mutable; codepath and field conditions remain specific to each entry.
sources.applicability: Supports a version-scoped encoding/round-trip concern and proposed tests; it is not evidence that a selected current binary passes them.

sources.title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata, Version 3.0
sources.publisher: PREMIS Editorial Committee / Library of Congress
sources.locator: Introduction pp. 18-19 (structural/derivation relationships, identified objects, relationship type and possible event); data dictionary pp. 117-120
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Library of Congress PDF and inspected relationship explanations and dictionary entries.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: PREMIS models preservation metadata and requires identified related objects and a characterized relationship when represented; a related event may be associated. The draft treats it as a model, not a requirement to implement all PREMIS.
sources.applicability: Supports stable lineage links among source audio, transcript versions and derivatives without requiring a small pilot to adopt PREMIS wholesale.

sources.title: Making Audio and Video Media Accessible
sources.publisher: World Wide Web Consortium, Web Accessibility Initiative
sources.version_or_commit: Live WAI guidance page; no release or commit identifier exposed in this check
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official W3C WAI guidance page and inspected transcript and player guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guidance addresses making audio/video media accessible; it is not a local player or transcript conformance result.
sources.applicability: Supports accessibility recommendations for a future listening/access experience, not claims about tested behavior.

sources.title: Planning Audio and Video Media
sources.publisher: World Wide Web Consortium, Web Accessibility Initiative
sources.version_or_commit: Live WAI planning guidance page; no release or commit identifier exposed in this check
sources.locator: Audio/video checklists, lines 114-139 in retrieved page (accessible media player and separate transcript for prerecorded audio-only media at Level A)
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official planning page and inspected checklist distinctions by audio-only/video and prerecorded/live content.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The checklist distinguishes WCAG Level A/AA/AAA requirements from needs beyond WCAG and applies transcript levels according to prerecorded versus live and audio-only versus video content.
sources.applicability: Supports retaining a separate transcript and accessible player as an optional proposed path for prerecorded audio-only material. It does not validate a particular player, transcript or access policy.
